headline: High: OpenMetadata can feed Opik via APIs/MCP while Opik has broad egress, creating default-path data leakage and cascading trust risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP, APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks, so its outputs can be consumed by Opik through a shared integration surface. Opik only advertises REST API and broad egress, with no provenance or parser hardening shown. This is not provably a direct instruction channel, but the shared surface makes injection plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Opik ingests OpenMetadata webhook/event payloads as instructions or prompts
IF a shared MCP or API bridge forwards untrusted catalog text into Opik without sanitization
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from OpenMetadata payloads
Add allowlist parsing for fields forwarded into Opik
Strip instruction-like text from webhook/event bodies
Log and review first 10 cross-agent payloads
requires-engineering: add provenance tags end-to-end

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/trust data, while Opik has broad network egress. If the pair shares a workspace or API bridge, sensitive metadata can flow from OpenMetadata into Opik and then out to third-party services. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata exports catalog or lineage records into Opik runs
IF Opik forwards received context to external endpoints under broad egress
mitigations: Restrict Opik egress to approved domains
Redact governance and lineage fields before export
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for integration tests
Turn off automatic file/context upload in the bridge
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based routing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and can call APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks; Opik exposes a REST API. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so a direct conflict is not established. Any conflict would require an explicit shared target or orchestrator, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external API resource without locking
IF the orchestrator maps both agents onto one mutable project or dataset
mitigations: Assign separate projects or namespaces
Disable concurrent writes during sync jobs
Add optimistic-lock checks on shared records
Run a quick dry-run to detect write collisions
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata produces governance and lineage outputs that Opik could treat as evaluation inputs or render into downstream reports. Opik's broad egress increases the chance that an unverified OpenMetadata output becomes an externally acted-on artifact. There is no evidence of built-in verification between them, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF Opik consumes OpenMetadata-generated metadata as authoritative input
IF downstream reports or actions are produced without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review step before export
Require schema validation on OpenMetadata outputs
Mark OpenMetadata fields as untrusted in Opik
Compare sampled records against source-of-truth systems
requires-engineering: add verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata explicitly touches governance and memory/trust data, but the profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch for either agent. Opik is unverified and has broad egress, so compliance risk exists if regulated data is routed through it, but the specific breach pathway is not documented. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pairwise flow.
conditions: IF regulated data from OpenMetadata is routed through Opik
IF Opik sends that data to a jurisdiction or processor not approved for the data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the integration path
Review Opik egress destinations
Document retention and deletion handling for shared data
Use synthetic data for testing
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
